mobile.computers.add.note: Button that starts setting up another computer. Sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.added.stays_listed.note: Follows "Connected to <computer>." after a newly added computer comes online. Reassures that the previous computer is still listed.

mobile.computers.badge.active.note: Lower-case monospace badge on a Settings computer row that is the connected one. Keep it lower case and one word to match the sibling badge.

mobile.computers.badge.connecting.note: Lower-case monospace badge on a Settings computer row whose connection is being made. Keep it lower case and one word to match the sibling badge.

mobile.computers.connecting.note: Inline status beside a computer row while its connection is being made. Keep the ellipsis character; one word plus ellipsis.

mobile.computers.none_on_phone.note: Empty state of the computer switcher when no computer has been paired on this phone. Ends with a full stop.

mobile.computers.password_placeholder.note: Placeholder of the password field. "lop mobile" is a command typed in a terminal: keep it verbatim in every language.

mobile.computers.section.not_connected.note: Section header for computers that belong to the reader's Radient account but are not paired on this phone. "Radient" is a product name: do not translate.

mobile.computers.section.on_phone.note: Section header for computers already paired on this phone.

mobile.computers.sign_out.note: Settings action opening the sign-out confirmation. Sentence case.

mobile.computers.signing_out.note: Pending label on the disabled Settings sign-out button while device removal and credential cleanup finish; may last up to 35 seconds. Keep the ellipsis.

mobile.computers.switch.note: Button (and the title of the sheet it opens) that lets the reader pick a different computer. Sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.session_error.note: Tunnel connection failure or protected reachability. App response-contract failures stay in-app; only explicit billing/disabled/harness server refusals direct the reader to a concrete console setting. Account404 cannot distinguish another owner from a deleted record; never invent device approval. Technical class names are redacted support data, not translated.

mobile.computers.transport.radient.note: Brand name for how a computer is reached, shown before its health word in the computer switcher as "Radient ● Online" (the status dot follows it). A product name: keep it as written.

mobile.computers.transport.custom.note: How a computer is reached when the user typed its address themselves (not through Radient). Shown on the switcher row's second line before the health dot, under a title that is the address itself, e.g. "127.0.0.1:18961" over "Your address ● Online"; also spoken as "Your address, <host>". Short noun phrase, sentence case.

mobile.computers.connect_refused.title.note: Title of an inline error on the "Your own tunnel" screen, shown when Save and connect was refused. The screen stays open with the address and password still filled in. Short, sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.connect_refused.generic.note: Body of the "Couldn't connect" error when the computer gave no more specific reason. Reassures the user that what they typed is kept, and tells them to check it and retry (a Retry button follows).

mobile.computers.connect_refused.passwor.note: Body of the "Couldn't connect" error when the relay on the user's computer rejected the relay password (HTTP 401). Tells the user what was wrong and the next step; a Retry button follows. "Relay" is the program on the user's computer that the app connects to.

mobile.computers.storage_refused.with_co.note: Shown when the phone's own secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore) refused to read, delete or save the app's sign-in data. {code} is a technical platform code such as "ERR_KEY_CHAIN -34018" for support: keep it exactly as written, untranslated, inside the parentheses. "Reinstall the app" is the remedy when retrying keeps failing.

mobile.computers.storage_refused.no_code.note: Same message as mobile.computers.storage_refused.with_code when the platform gave no code: the phone's own secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore) refused the request.

mobile.computers.save_refused.title.note: Title of a warning on the "Your own tunnel" screen: the connection succeeded, but the phone's secure storage refused to save the address and password, so they are lost when the app restarts. Short, sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.save_refused.body.note: Body of the "Connected, but not saved" warning: the connection succeeded, but the phone's own secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore) would not keep the address and password, so they must be typed again after the app restarts. The only button is Continue, so do not suggest trying again.

mobile.computers.save_refused.body_with_.note: Same message as mobile.computers.save_refused.body when the platform gave a code. {code} is a technical platform code such as "ERR_KEY_CHAIN -34018" for support: keep it exactly as written, untranslated, inside the parentheses.

mobile.computers.save_refused.continue.note: Button in the "Connected, but not saved" warning that continues to the home screen. One word, sentence case.

mobile.computers.wait.nothing_answered.note: Heading of the add-a-computer wait panel when the three-minute wait ended with no tunnel listed and no host answering. A short sentence with a final full stop; a follow-up help line sits under it.

mobile.computers.wait.nothing_answered_h.note: Continuation line under the "Nothing answered." heading of the add-a-computer wait panel: explains that three minutes passed with no tunnel listed and no host answering, then tells the user to check the command ran on the computer and start again. Two sentences; the second is the instruction.

mobile.computers.wait.paused.note: Wait-panel line shown when the app was backgrounded during the add-a-computer wait and polling stopped. Two short sentences; the second is the instruction to reopen the app.

mobile.computers.wait.relay_version_sess.note: Wait-panel line once the computer answered: the relay's protocol version and its running-session count. {version} is a number, {sessions} a count; preserve the ICU plural arms and both placeholders. 'Relay' is the product's name for the program on the computer.

mobile.computers.wait.relay_version.note: Wait-panel line once the computer answered and only the protocol version is known. {version} is a number; preserve the placeholder.

mobile.computers.wait.relay_sessions.note: Wait-panel line once the computer answered and only the running-session count is known. {sessions} is a count; preserve the ICU plural arms.

mobile.computers.wait.host_answering.note: Help line in the add-a-computer wait panel once Radient lists the computer's host name. {host} is a host name; keep it unchanged and left-to-right. The second sentence explains that a listed route does not prove the computer is running.

mobile.computers.wait.answering.note: Help line in the add-a-computer wait panel before a host name is known. Ends with a full stop.

mobile.computers.added.fallback_name.note: Fallback name spliced into "Connected to <name>." when the added computer's own name is unknown. Lower case, a noun phrase that fits after "Connected to".

mobile.computers.added.connected_to.note: Status line in the add-a-computer panel once the new computer answers. {name} is the computer's own name, or the fallback_name noun phrase, which must fit after "Connected to". Ends with a full stop; keep {name} unchanged.

mobile.computers.not_harness.note: Muted line on a computer row in the Your computers list when the account lists the computer but it is not running the Local Operator harness. Full sentence with a full stop. 'Local Operator' is the product name: keep it in Latin script.

mobile.computers.wait.listing.note: First step of the add-a-computer wait panel (shimmering line): the app is waiting for Radient to show the new computer in the account. Ends with an ellipsis, no full stop.

mobile.computers.wait.tunnel_status.note: Second step of the add-a-computer wait panel. {status} is a LOCALISED status label chosen by tunnel-status-key.ts from Radient's own tunnel-status word (active -> mobile.computers.badge.active; provisioning, suspended, disabled, revoked and unknown -> mobile.computers.status.*). It is a lower-case predicate word placed after the dash, so the sentence must read naturally with a lower-case word or short phrase there. Ends with a full stop; keep {status} unchanged.

mobile.computers.wait.answered.note: Third step of the add-a-computer wait panel: the computer responded. Full sentence with a full stop.

mobile.computers.wait.use_computer.note: Primary button under the add-a-computer wait panel once the computer answered; switches the app to it. Imperative, short.

mobile.computers.wait.start_again.note: Quiet button under the add-a-computer wait panel that abandons the wait and returns to the start of the setup. Short imperative.

mobile.computers.refresh.note: Small quiet button under the Your computers list that re-reads the account's computers. One verb. Same English as mobile.settings.connection.refresh but a separate key because the surface differs.

mobile.computers.list.heading.note: Section header above the list of computers on the Radient account on the computers screen. Plural noun phrase, no punctuation.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel_instead.note: Small quiet button at the bottom of the computers screen that opens the own-tunnel (self-hosted) setup instead of Radient. 'instead' contrasts with the Radient list above it.

mobile.computers.remove.title.note: Title of the confirmation dialog for removing a computer from this phone. A question. Body and buttons are separate strings.

mobile.computers.remove.body.note: Body of the remove-computer confirmation, under 'Remove this computer?'. States the removal is local to this phone only; keep all three negations (the computer, its tunnel, the account). Two sentences, each with a full stop.

mobile.computers.paths.radient_title.note: Title of the Radient card on the choose-a-path screen, followed on the same line by the 'Recommended' badge. Imperative phrase, no punctuation; 'Radient' is the brand: keep it in Latin script.

mobile.computers.paths.recommended.note: Badge beside the Radient card title marking it as the suggested path. One word or short phrase; not a status.

mobile.computers.paths.radient_body.note: Description inside the Radient card on the choose-a-path screen. Three clauses: needs an account; Radient runs the tunnel and gives a private authenticated URL; nothing to configure on the phone and no relay password. Keep the honest cost (an account is needed). 'URL' stays as a technical token.

mobile.computers.paths.own_title.note: Section header of the own-tunnel card on the choose-a-path screen, and the quiet button label on the first-run welcome screen that opens the same setup, and the outline button in Settings that opens the own-tunnel editor when none is saved. Says what the reader gets, not what they type. No punctuation.

mobile.computers.paths.own_body.note: Description inside the own-tunnel card. It is the advanced, self-hosted path: the reader publishes the computer through their own tunnel, pastes its address, needs no Radient account and keeps the password. Keep the words 'advanced' and 'no account' clear.

mobile.computers.paths.own_action.note: Outline button in the own-tunnel card that opens the own-tunnel setup. Short imperative; the computers screen has a separate 'Use my own tunnel instead'.

mobile.computers.status.route_ready.note: Lower-case monospace badge on a computer row in the Your computers list: the control plane says the route to this computer is ready. Reads as a status of the route, not of the computer. Keep lower case; sibling of the other status.* badges.

mobile.computers.status.provisioning.note: Lower-case badge on a computer row: the control plane is still setting the computer's route up. Keep lower case, one word or short phrase.

mobile.computers.status.suspended.note: Lower-case badge on a computer row: Radient has suspended the tunnel (for example billing). Keep lower case.

mobile.computers.status.disabled.note: Lower-case badge on a computer row: remote access for this tunnel is switched off. Keep lower case.

mobile.computers.status.revoked.note: Lower-case badge on a computer row: the tunnel's access was revoked. Keep lower case.

mobile.computers.status.unknown.note: Lower-case badge on a computer row: the status is not known. Keep lower case.

mobile.computers.reach.answering.note: Lower-case badge on a computer row: this phone probed the computer and it answered. Distinct from status.*: it is the probe result. Keep lower case.

mobile.computers.row.a11y.note: Screen-reader label of a computer row (not visible). {name} is the computer's own name, {status} the status badge text (status.*), {reach} the reachability badge text. Keep the three comma-separated parts in this order; keep all placeholders unchanged.

mobile.computers.row.a11y_active.note: Screen-reader label of the computer row that is the connected one. Same placeholders as row.a11y; ends with the word for 'active' (same word as badge.active).

mobile.computers.row.a11y_connecting.note: Screen-reader label of a computer row while its connection is being made. Same placeholders as row.a11y; ends with the word for 'connecting' (same word as badge.connecting).

mobile.computers.billing_inactive.note: Warning line on a computer row when the account's billing for the tunnel is inactive and the server supplied no message of its own. Full sentence with a full stop.

mobile.computers.try_now.note: Action button inside the warning banner shown when computer discovery failed; re-runs discovery immediately. Short imperative.

mobile.computers.remove.confirm.note: Destructive confirm button of the 'Remove this computer?' dialog. One verb; the dialog also has the shared Cancel.

mobile.computers.title.list.note: Screen title of the Computers screen when it lists the account's computers (or is loading or showing an error). One or two words; the header is narrow on phones, so keep it short. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.title.set_up.note: Screen title of the Computers screen when it shows how to add a computer (the account has none, or the reader chose Add a computer). Imperative, sentence case, short: the header is narrow on phones. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.banner.unreachable_stal.note: Warning banner above the computer list when Radient (the account service, a brand name: keep it) did not answer and the list shown is from before. Also shown under the computers in Settings. Never promises an automatic retry; a Try now button sits beside it.

mobile.computers.banner.unreachable_empt.note: Warning banner on the Computers screen when Radient (brand name: keep it) did not answer and no computers are known yet. Points the reader at this phone's network. Never promises an automatic retry; a Try now button sits beside it.

mobile.computers.banner.unreadable_stale.note: Warning banner above the computer list when Radient (brand name: keep it) answered with something the app could not understand, and the list shown is from before. Also shown in Settings. Never promises an automatic retry.

mobile.computers.banner.unreadable_empty.note: Warning banner on the Computers screen when Radient (brand name: keep it) answered with something the app could not understand and no computers are known yet. Never promises an automatic retry.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.title.note: Screen title on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). Short: the header is narrow on phones. No final full stop. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.password_for.note: Heading on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) when the phone already knows the computer and only its password is missing. {name} is the computer's name as the reader saved it; keep it unchanged. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.password_lab.note: Visible label and accessible name of the password field on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). The relay is the small server on the reader's computer that the app talks to. Two or three words, no final full stop. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.intro.note: Opening paragraph on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). Radient is a brand name: keep it. The relay is the small server on the reader's computer; a tunnel is a service that gives it a public address.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_compute.note: Step 1 heading on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); a fixed numeral "1." is shown before it, so do not add a number. Says this step happens on the reader's computer, not the phone. No final full stop.

Help under step 1 on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), above terminal commands. "Binds loopback only" means the relay accepts connections from the same computer only. Keep it plain.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_publish.note: Step 2 heading on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); a fixed numeral "2." is shown before it, so do not add a number. "It" is the relay: make it reachable from the internet through a tunnel. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_app.note: Step 3 heading on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); a fixed numeral "3." is shown before it, so do not add a number. This step is the address and password fields in this app. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.url_label.note: Visible label and accessible name of the address field on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account): the tunnel's public web address. The example placeholder inside the field is not translated. No final full stop. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_all.note: Toggle button on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) that opts in to an unencrypted address. "http://" is the literal scheme: keep it unchanged and left-to-right. No final full stop. In ur the http(s) scheme token is wrapped in LRI…PDI (U+2066/U+2069), because without it the RTL paragraph reorders it to "//:http"; this is a recorded mobile-only exception to the no-bidi-controls rule (programme manager ruling, M3 S2a). Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

Label of the same toggle once the opt-in is on on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "http://" is the literal scheme: keep it unchanged. No final full stop. In ur the http(s) scheme token is wrapped in LRI…PDI (U+2066/U+2069), because without it the RTL paragraph reorders it to "//:http"; this is a recorded mobile-only exception to the no-bidi-controls rule (programme manager ruling, M3 S2a). Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_hin.note: Screen-reader hint (not shown on screen) of the plain-http toggle on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "http" is the protocol name: keep it. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_on_.note: Line under the plain-http toggle while it is ON on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). Starts by stating the toggle's state; a warning, keep it direct.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_off.note: Line under the plain-http toggle while it is OFF on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "http://" and "https://" are literal schemes: keep them unchanged and left-to-right. "It" is the opt-in. In ur the http(s) scheme token is wrapped in LRI…PDI (U+2066/U+2069), because without it the RTL paragraph reorders it to "//:http"; this is a recorded mobile-only exception to the no-bidi-controls rule (programme manager ruling, M3 S2a).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.unencrypted_.note: Title of a warning box on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) when the typed address starts with http:// and the opt-in is off. Short, no final full stop.

Body of the unencrypted-address warning on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "The opt-in" is the plain-http toggle just above. "https://" is a literal scheme: keep it unchanged and left-to-right. In ur the http(s) scheme token is wrapped in LRI…PDI (U+2066/U+2069), because without it the RTL paragraph reorders it to "//:http"; this is a recorded mobile-only exception to the no-bidi-controls rule (programme manager ruling, M3 S2a).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.private_host.note: Warning line on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) when plain http is allowed and the address is a private (home or office network) one.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.public_host.note: Warning line on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) when plain http is allowed and the address is reachable on the public internet. Keep the warning strong.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_test.note: Step 4 heading on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); a fixed numeral "4." is shown before it, so do not add a number. "It" is the connection. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_test_he.note: Help under step 4 on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), above the Test the connection button.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.security_hea.note: Section heading of the security advice at the end on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "It" is the reader's computer. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.security_bod.note: Security advice paragraph on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). {command} is a terminal command (lop mobile password): keep the placeholder and its backticks unchanged. HTTPS and URL are technical terms; keep them recognisable.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.test.note: Button on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) that makes a real request through the tunnel. Sentence case, no final full stop. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.testing.note: The same button's label while the test request runs on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). Keep the ellipsis character; one word plus ellipsis. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.save_connect.note: Button on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) that stores the address and password on this phone and connects. Enabled only after a successful test. Sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.saving.note: The same button's label while saving and connecting on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). Keep the ellipsis character; one word plus ellipsis.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.need_address.note: Line under the buttons on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) while the address field is empty, explaining why Save and connect is disabled.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.need_test.note: Line under the buttons on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) when an address is typed but no test has succeeded, explaining why Save and connect is disabled. "Test the connection" names the button above; translate it the same way.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_ok.note: Title of the success box after Test the connection on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account): the relay answered. One word, no final full stop. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_not_.note: Title of the failure box after Test the connection on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account): the test did not reach a working relay; the sentence below names which step is wrong. Short and calm, no final full stop. Also used, with the same meaning, in the "Your own tunnel" section of Settings (editing the saved own-tunnel).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.install_labe.note: Small upper-case label above a copyable command block on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), step "On the computer". The command under it is `lop mobile install` (macOS). Under it the app shows the exact command, copied verbatim; the command is never translated. Short, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.foreground_l.note: Small upper-case label above a copyable command block on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account): the alternative to installing, running the relay in a terminal window ("foreground" as opposed to a background service). Under it the app shows the exact command, copied verbatim; the command is never translated. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.check_label.note: Small upper-case label above a copyable command block on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); the command (`lop mobile status`) reports whether the relay is healthy. Under it the app shows the exact command, copied verbatim; the command is never translated. Short imperative, no final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.rotate_label.note: Small upper-case label above a copyable command block on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); the command (`lop mobile password`) sets a new relay password. "Rotate" means replace with a new one. Under it the app shows the exact command, copied verbatim; the command is never translated. No final full stop.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.install_note.note: One sentence under the "Install on the computer" command on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "macOS" is the operating system name: keep it as is. "Daemon" is a background service that is restarted if it stops; "keychain" is the macOS password store (use the term Apple uses in your language).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.foreground_n.note: One sentence under the "Or run it in the foreground" command on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). {address} is a fixed local network address and port (127.0.0.1:4098): never translated, keep it left-to-right. "Loopback only" means reachable from this same computer only.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.check_note.note: One phrase under the "Check it" command on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), listing what the command reports. "Auth gate" is the password check in front of the relay.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.rotate_note.note: Two sentences under the "Set or rotate the password" command on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "Shell history" and "process list" are the places a typed command line is recorded on a computer; use the usual technical terms in your language.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.cloudflare_n.note: One sentence under the Cloudflare tunnel command on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account); the block's label is the product name "Cloudflare" and stays untranslated. {scheme} is the literal URL scheme "https://": never translated, keep it left-to-right.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.ngrok_note.note: One sentence under the ngrok tunnel command on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account). "ngrok" is a product name: keep it exactly, lower case, in Latin script. {scheme} is the literal URL scheme "https://": never translated, keep it left-to-right.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.tunnel_rule.note: One sentence above the two example tunnel commands on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), for a reader who uses another tunnel provider. "HTTPS" is the protocol name: keep it. {address} is a fixed local network address and port (127.0.0.1:4098): never translated, keep it left-to-right.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_sess.note: Body of the success box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: the relay answered and {sessions} is how many conversations the phone can see. ICU plural: keep the {sessions, plural, ...} structure and the # in every arm; add the plural arms your language needs.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_pass.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: the relay refused the password. Plain, no apology.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_forb.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: something in front of the relay refused the request. {address} is a fixed local network address and port (127.0.0.1:4098): never translated, keep it left-to-right. Origin = the requesting site/app; the relay refuses cross-origin requests.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_offl.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings, when the relay's server sent its own reason. {detail} is that reason, sent by the server in English and shown as is (it has no final full stop, which is why the message adds one). {command} is a command to run on the computer (`lop mobile status`): never translated, keep it left-to-right. Keep both sentences; adjust the separator to your language's punctuation.

Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: the public tunnel is up but the relay on the computer is not running. {command} is a command to run on the computer (`lop mobile status`): never translated, keep it left-to-right.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_tls.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: the HTTPS certificate failed verification. {scheme} is the literal URL scheme "https://": never translated, keep it left-to-right.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_host.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: the address's host name does not resolve (DNS).

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_unre.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: no connection could be made to the address.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_time.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: the request timed out. {seconds} is the time limit (today 10). ICU plural: keep the {seconds, plural, ...} structure and the # in every arm; add the plural arms your language needs.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_loca.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings, on iPhone, for an address on the reader's own network. The permission is a POSSIBILITY, not the diagnosed cause: keep "may". "Local Operator" is the app's name: keep it exactly, in Latin script. "Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network" is Apple's own menu path: use the labels iOS itself shows in your language, keeping the arrows. {action} is the label of the "Test the connection" button, already translated.

Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings, on Android and the web, for an address on the reader's own network. {action} is the label of the "Test the connection" button, already translated.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_refu.note: Body of the failure box after "Test the connection" on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) and in Settings: something answered, but it is not a Local Operator relay.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.remedy.note: A separate line under the failure box on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account) when the relay is not running: what to run on the computer. {command} is a command (`lop mobile status`): never translated, keep it left-to-right.

mobile.computers.own_tunnel.password_slo.note: Help under the password field on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), when the phone's single saved password belongs to a different computer.
Help under the password field on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), when no password is saved on the phone yet.
Help under the password field on the "Your own tunnel" screen (connect to a relay you publish yourself, no Radient account), when the phone's saved password already belongs to this address.

mobile.computers.setup.open_settings.note: First line of the set-up screen for a signed-in account with no computer yet. The arrows are a menu path in the desktop app (Settings, then the Radient account section, then its Phone access block); translate "Settings", "Radient account", "Phone access" and "Set up" exactly as the desktop app does.

mobile.computers.setup.list_updates.note: Follows the set-up instruction. While this screen is open the phone checks for the new computer every few seconds, and again when the reader returns to the screen or the app; a 'Check again' button sits below.

mobile.computers.setup.check_again.note: Button on the 'Set up a computer' screen. Lists the account's computers again right now, for a reader who just finished phone-access set-up on their computer.

mobile.computers.setup.checking.note: Replaces the 'Check again' button label while the phone asks Radient for the account's computers.

mobile.computers.hint.radient_unreachabl.note: Hint under a computer row in the switcher when the phone could not reach Radient (Radient's error, the phone's network, or rate limiting). It must not suggest the computer is asleep.
